data.description:
## Context

A read-based cognitive-complexity/documentation audit (independently verified twice: once by
the auditing agent, once by the operator) found a single consistent defect class across
~143,000 LOC: comments and docstrings that were true when written and are now false. These are
disproportionately costly for LLM agents, which treat a comment as authoritative, follow a
pointer to a symbol that no longer exists, and burn context recovering.

This ticket is scoped to 9 specific, independently-verified sites plus a read-only census of a
10th "Parser of record" family that is explicitly excluded from editing. The change is
**behaviour-preserving**: comment/docstring corrections, two statement moves (same file, no
semantic change), one dead-assignment deletion, and one new self-checking test. No control flow
changes.

## Sites (re-verify each against current origin/main before editing; audit base was 2e28d817a7e)

1. `src/rebar/llm/code_review/finalize.py` ~12-30 and the constant-block comment: the module
   docstring/comment says `_STEP_VERIFY`/`_STEP_DECIDE`/`_LLM_STEP_KINDS` mirror
   `gate_dispatch.py`. `gate_dispatch.py` defines none of those three names. The real canonical
   home is `src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py` (`STEP_VERIFY` L20, `STEP_DECIDE`
   L21, `_LLM_STEP_KINDS` L70). A third copy of `_LLM_STEP_KINDS` exists at
   `src/rebar/llm/workflow/runs.py:393` with a differently-worded trailing comment. Fix: correct
   both comments in `finalize.py` to name `plan_review_recovery` as canonical, note the `runs.py`
   copy exists, and preserve the stated reason for the duplication (keeping `finalize.py` a
   strict leaf with no back-import). Add a test asserting `finalize.py`'s constants equal
   `plan_review_recovery.py`'s, and that the `runs.py` copy equals them too — placed in the
   existing test module that is the natural home (look before creating a new file).

2. `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py` ~21-23 (`_NON_GRAPH_ARTIFACT_TYPES = ("session_log",
   "code_review", "identity")`, 3 members) and ~247-255: the comment names only 2 types
   (`identity` was added by b665cff905d without updating prose). 4 further sites inherited the
   stale 2-type claim: `src/rebar/reducer/_api.py` ~247-255, `src/rebar/graph/_ready.py` ~92-94,
   `src/rebar/graph/_unblock.py` ~167-170, `src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py` ~86-88. Fix: correct
   all 5 to refer to the tuple by name rather than enumerating members in prose (follow
   `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:421-424`'s existing correct pattern). Do not change
   `export_ndjson`'s behaviour — whether identity tickets should be exported is a separate open
   question for the operator.

3. `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py`: ~65 references a
   nonexistent `_OUTBOUND_UPDATE_ALLOWLIST` (sole occurrence repo-wide is this comment) — restate
   accurately from surrounding code or delete. ~415 claims `_index_existing_links` is
   "duplicated" from `apply_outbound` but only one definition exists repo-wide (~412, 3 lines
   below) — delete the false claim. Also independently check two audit-flagged-but-unverified
   sites in this package: `outbound_pass.py:282-284` (claims `set_relationship` and
   `payload["links"]` live in `apply_outbound.py`) and `applier.py:100,111-118,120`. Fix if
   genuinely dangling; report as sound otherwise.

4. `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/decide.py` ~681-684: `_sev = severity_label(imp)` is justified
   as keeping `severity_label` "exercised/live", but `severity_label` (defined L621) is exported
   and independently tested, and `_sev` is never read. Delete the statement and its false
   comment. File is at 782/800 LOC — net change must be negative, not neutral or positive.

5. `src/rebar/llm/workflow/interpreter.py` ~252-259: `_commit_state`'s docstring claims it is
   "the single chokepoint" serializing every write. Verified: 9 state-write sites in the file,
   7 of which bypass `_commit_state`, including the two the docstring names by hand. Re-verify
   the write-site census against current source, then correct the docstring to describe only
   what's actually guaranteed and verified — do not guess at an unverified mechanism for how the
   broader invariant is actually maintained.

6. `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`: `tests/unit/test_step_failures.py` ~241-255 slices
   the module's raw source text between `def _run_code_review_gate` and `def
   _consumed_diagnostic` — making those two names' existence and relative order load-bearing in a
   way invisible to any rename tool or semantic index. Add a short comment at both ends (the
   definitions in `gate_dispatch.py`, matching the load-bearing-note style already at ~34-40; and
   the slicing code in the test) stating the coupling and naming the other end. File at 777/800
   LOC — keep the source-side note to 1-2 lines.

7. `src/rebar/_engine_support/next_batch.py`: (a) move the `_blocked_ids` binding (~244) and its
   explanatory comment to above the parent-story gate helpers that read it (~229), verifying
   `open_blockers_by_ticket` isn't bound later than the new position. (b) `files_read`
   (`__slots__` ~61, initialized to `set()` ~77) is never assigned anywhere in the repo; it's
   emitted under the different name `files_likely_read` (~345), which is why nobody caught it. It
   is a published schema field (`src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json`, `src/rebar/types.py`,
   pinned to `[]` by 2 tests) — do not remove it. Add a comment at the initialization explaining
   it's retained for output/schema compatibility, matching the style of the
   `skipped_needs_planning` note ~160 lines below, and mentioning the `files_read` →
   `files_likely_read` rename that hid it.

8. `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py`: `_read_or` is called ~214-215 but defined last in the
   file (~330) — pure reading-order issue (module-level, resolves fine at call time). Move its
   definition above the first caller.

9. `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/floors.py`: `_recompute_verdict_after_drop`
   (`drift_floor.py:200`) is called from `drift_floor.py:286`, `xcheck.py:180`, `xcheck.py:310`.
   `floors.py` has 2 appliers of the same drop-a-finding algorithm but calls it from neither, and
   never explains why (unlike `xcheck.py`, which does). Read both `floors.py` appliers and
   `_recompute_verdict_after_drop` and determine whether the omission is correct. If correct
   (e.g. floors path cannot change the verdict), add a one-line note saying so. If NOT correct,
   that is a behavioural bug, OUT OF SCOPE for this change — do not fix it, report it clearly
   instead and leave the code alone.

10. (Read-only census, do not edit) The "Parser of record" family: ~14-21 modules carry a
    "Parser of record" comment above an argparse factory whose result is discarded. Pin the exact
    count of files containing the literal string, list them with line numbers, and for each say
    whether the parsed result is used or discarded. Resolve the discrepancy between the audit's
    count (21 sites / 15 discarding) and the operator's recount (14 literals).

## Acceptance criteria

- Each of sites 1-9 is re-verified against current `origin/main` before editing; if a site no
  longer matches its description, it is skipped and reported, not forced.
- Site 1 includes a new plain test function (no new test helper/fixture) asserting the 3-way
  constant mirror.
- Sites 2-9 contain only comment/docstring corrections, the 2 described statement moves (7a,
  7b is a comment-only change), and the single dead-statement deletion in site 4 — no control
  flow changes anywhere.
- `decide.py` and `gate_dispatch.py` line counts are net-neutral or lower after the change.
- No new config key, env var, feature flag, CI gate, lock, autouse fixture, or test helper is
  introduced (mechanism-delta ratchet stays clean).
- `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` passes with no new/increased entries.
- `make verify` passes from a fresh worktree with the worktree venv first on PATH.
- The item-10 census is reported (file list + line numbers + used-vs-discarded), with no edits
  made to any of those files.
- Item 3's two audit-flagged-but-unverified cross-references in `outbound_pass.py` and
  `applier.py` are independently checked and the verdict (dangling vs sound) is reported.
- Item 9: if `floors.py`'s omission turns out to be a real behavioural bug, it is reported
  separately and NOT fixed in this change.
- Change pushed to `git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main`, not submitted — human operator submits
  after reviewing `LLM-Review`/`Verified` votes.
data.title: Fix 9 stale comment/docstring sites from read-based audit (finalize.py, _api.py, dispatch_apply_phases.py, decide.py, interpreter.py, gate_dispatch.py, next_batch.py, fsck_recover.py, floors.py)
